_comment: A lone undisciplined 53-man Spearmen block nine files wide (five full ranks and a rear rank of eight), facing north at (520, 480). Its move order east to (620, 500) snaps it round onto the new heading, and a queued waypoint north to (640, 400) snaps it back the other way; the two snaps leave its grid skewed about 14 degrees off the heading when it halts. At tick 600 V about-faces it in place, which composes the drill's 180 degrees onto that skew (about 166 degrees in all, off a half-turn). At tick 800 a move order south, the way it now faces, re-squares the grid. The drills under the fold net a half-turn, so the re-square reflects it in depth like any about-face: the men turn only through the 14 degree skew and the short files step up a rank, and the block marches off whole. Before, the angle-only test read the fold as no about-face, and dropping it swung the grid 166 degrees under the men: DemoDefects over ticks 8-1500 reads path_crossing 0.47 and shape_residual 35.2 on main against 0.0 and 2.7 here, and on main 40 of 53 men cross the block's centreline to the other flank. Drill mode: no enemy.
